Physics, Minor
Physics is the most fundamental of the sciences, and undergraduate training in physics provides a solid grounding in
quantitative problem solving, analytical reasoning, and mathematical modeling. Fundamental knowledge of physics is relevant
to a wide variety of majors and careers. A minor in physics is designed for students who have an interest in the fundamental
laws of nature, the basic properties of matter, and the nature of space and time.
The physics minor begins with the foundational sequence, Physics 1 and 2, each with their respective labs. Students then take
any three additional physics courses, two of which must be upper division (PX 3000 or higher).
Requirements for the Minor in Physics
Students must take at least 17 credits, distributed as follows:
A. Foundational Courses: 8 Credits
For Physics 1 and 2, students may take either the Calculus Track or the Algebra Track. The Calculus Track is recom‐
mended for chemistry, math, and computer science majors, as well as any other science majors and pre-health students
who have taken or are enrolled in calculus.
Calculus Track
PX 2200 - Physics 1, Calculus-based Credits: 3
PX 2201 - Physics 1, Calculus-based lab Credits: 1
PX 2300 - Physics 2, Calculus-based Credits: 3
PX 2301 - Physics 2, Calculus-based Lab Credits: 1
Algebra Track
PX 2000 - Physics 1, Algebra-based Credits: 3
PX 2001 - Physics 1, Algebra Based Lab Credits: 1
PX 2100 - Physics 2, Algebra-based Credits: 3
PX 2101 - Physics 2, Algebra-based Lab Credits: 1
B. Elective Courses: 9 credits
